Source of truth for this file's SHAPE and gates: docs/decisions/0176-...-made-real.md D5.
Generator: scripts/gen-authz-matrix-cells.mjs   Emits: authz_enforcement_manifest.psql
Catalog binding: supabase/tests/410_ae49_d5_enforcement_manifest.sql (post-reset pgTAP).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. 401 § 19 used to map 43 permission codes to their legacy gate with a
`CASE ... ELSE 'is_staff_admin_of_for'`. That ELSE sent 38 of 43 codes to one gate, so a 44th
permission would have INHERITED a mapping instead of forcing a decision. Every row here is
explicit; there is no wildcard key, no `??` fallback on the generator's read path, and every
required field is read through a `req()` helper that THROWS when the key is absent. A 44th
permission breaks `npm run lint:authz-vectors` until someone names its enforcement path.
THE DIVISION OF LABOUR, AND WHY IT IS SPLIT THIS WAY (the binding constraint):
* `npm run lint` (gate 12) is PURE JSON. It must never require Docker. It checks that this
file is internally consistent, has no default arm, and agrees with `catalogSnapshot`.
* `supabase/tests/410_...sql` checks `catalogSnapshot` against the LIVE CATALOG, both set
differences, in a place where the DB is already up. That is where the catalog is truth.
Neither half alone closes the loop, and the snapshot is the seam between them: lint proves the
manifest matches the snapshot, 410 proves the snapshot matches the database.
PROVENANCE IS DECLARED PER FIELD, DELIBERATELY. Some of what a row declares is bound to the
catalog (`catalog.*`, asserted by 410); some is derived from a written architecture rule
(`axes.resourceLifecycle`); some is measured off a site body (`hardDenyClasses` where sites are
enumerated); and some is HONESTLY NOT YET KNOWABLE (`not-attributable-until-rekey`). Collapsing
those into one undifferentiated list would let an unmeasured field read exactly like a measured
one. The escape hatch is FENCED: `not-attributable-until-rekey` is admissible ONLY on a row with
zero enumerated sites AND a reviewed call-graph boundary, so it can never silence a row whose
sites are known.
⛔⛔ AND THE MEASURED LABEL CARRIES BOTH ITS BOUNDS IN ITS NAME — READ THEM BEFORE READING A
LIST OR A ZERO. `measured-transitive-over-gated-classes` (3 rows, 2026-09-07, ADR 0193 D2/D3)
means EXACTLY: the hard-deny vocabulary gates reachable from the enumerated site bodies and the
domain authorizer body through the COMPOSED-CALL CLOSURE, comment-stripped, with NO depth
bound — and over the 3 of 7 vocabulary classes that HAVE a gate to search for. It is a claim
about what is reachable by CALL, and it is silent about the four gate-less classes (two
triggers, the UUID id-space, ADR 0172's deferred column), which no call search can ever find.
⛔ THE VALUES ARE A COMMITTED CLAIM, hand-written and dated, never generated: the generator
does not open a database connection, so 410 § 6.2 compares this committed set against a set
derived from the LIVE catalog at run time. A value derived live and compared live would be a
number compared to itself (LEARN-084), and that property — not the SQL — is what makes § 6.2
an assertion at all.

_comment: HOW `axes.resourceLifecycle` WAS DERIVED, stated so a reader can check it instead of trusting

submitted) and document drafts. A permission that acts on none of those families takes

provenance `axis-vocabulary-inapplicable`. The ten permissions that DO act on those families
take their values from written architecture rules (Rule 3 lifecycle/resume, Rule 4 sign-offs

one field in a row that no gate can contradict; `po-approved` is reserved for when AE4.3-style
approval gives them an oracle.

⛔⛔ THE SECOND AUTHORITY MOVED, AND THIS ROW IS THE RECORD OF WHERE IT WENT.

app.is_tenancy_admin_of(...)`. AFTER it each policy is a single

asserts it is still inside the authorizer. Deleting it there is now the regression,

matching it as a CALL is what keeps a rename visible.
